column3: Your flight lands three hours late. AeroGuard pays on its own.

You buy cover with a signed status from the AeroDataBox Airnode on API3 AirnodeHub. After landing, a keeper buys the signed arrival over x402, the contract verifies it, and pays. Nobody files a claim.
The contract checks the Airnode's signature, rebuilds the request hash for this exact flight and date, and only sells cover before departure.
Our keeper decides when data is worth buying, pays five cents per signed answer, simulates the settlement, and sends it.
Every policy is live on Base Sepolia.
Each one closes on the Airnode's signed arrival. Two hours late or cancelled pays. Anything else closes with no payout. The data decides.
Now let's cheat. Anyone can attack the live contract, right from the browser.
An edited value, another flight's answer, an attacker's key, an old answer. All rejected by the real contract.
Ninety-four tests, including the full live lifecycle of our policies, replayed on their real Airnode signatures.
And every payout rule on a local chain, in seconds.
AeroGuard. No signature, no money moves.
